lesson-intro.text: Every town square needs a fountain. Ours has three basins stacked like cake plates, with water spilling from each. Watch it fill up, then pour your own.

rim.text: Start with the big basin: a wide flat oval, open at the back. A second curve runs just inside it.

basin-side.text: Its side hangs below the front, with straight ends and a long curve.

panels.text: Three orange panels line the side. The end ones look narrower as they turn away.

step.text: Under it all, a gray stone step, its flat top showing at each end.

blocks.text: Four short upright lines split the step into blocks.

column.text: A thick column rises from the water, flaring out at its foot. Behind it, the back of both ovals.

middle-basin.text: Up on the column, a smaller basin. A flat oval, open at the back, sits over a round bowl.

middle-ribs.text: Next, four ribs curve down the bowl.

top-basin.text: A short stem, then the top basin, the same shape but smaller.

top-ribs.text: Then a line under the rim, and four ribs like the ones below.

ball.text: On top, a little knob and a round ball.

water-top.text: Water spills from the ball in two small arcs. The back of the basin runs from each to the knob.

water-mid.text: Two more arcs pour from under the top basin. Again, the oval's back runs from each to the stem.

water-big.text: Four long arcs fall from the middle basin into the big one. First, the two from under the bowl.

water-outer.text: The outer two start behind the small arcs. Then fill in the rim between each pair.

ripples.text: Two ripples curve across the water below.

cream.text: Cream for the stone: the rim, the bowls, the stem and the ball.

blue.text: Blue for all the water, the arcs too.

gray.text: Gray for the step and the column.

lesson-outro.text: Your fountain is splashing away. Would you toss a coin in?
